decisions.title: Stable-line clarifications after 1.0.2
decisions.issue: The pinned 1.0.2 publication predates clarifications for reserved data names, JSON null and base64 handling, duplicate attributes, data-less events, Kafka tombstones, media-type comparison, and batch version consistency.
interpretations: adopt only reviewed clarifications that resolve the stable 1.0 contract and pin every selected commit
decisions.peer_behavior: Official SDKs evolve with stable-line clarifications at different release times, while the archived official conformance scenarios cover only selected HTTP and Kafka receiver behavior.
decisions.security_consequences: Narrow adoption prevents duplicate or colliding metadata and ambiguous payload interpretation without widening accepted input.
decisions.resource_consequences: byte, depth, attribute, header, and batch limits still apply.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Stable 1.0 messages receive one deterministic interpretation across JSON, HTTP, and Kafka.
decisions.wire_consequences: Messages relying on duplicate attributes or conflicting data members are rejected; no unreleased feature is emitted.
decisions.upstream_status: Accepted commits and their exact interpretation
decisions.reconsider_when: CloudEvents publishes a stable patch release that incorporates, reverses, or supersedes one of the selected clarifications.

decisions.title: Extension attribute-name compatibility
decisions.issue: Development text recommends that attribute names start with a letter, but the pinned 1.0.2 contract permits lowercase alphanumeric names and does not impose that first-character rule.
interpretations: preserve 1.0.2 validity until a supported released feature line changes it
decisions.peer_behavior: SDK validation may follow the specification revision bundled with each release.
decisions.selected_behavior: Names remain non-empty lowercase ASCII alphanumeric and may begin with a digit.
decisions.rationale: No peer default can retroactively change the package's pinned 1.0.2 contract.
decisions.security_consequences: The restricted character set avoids Unicode, case-folding, and normalization ambiguity.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Existing digit-leading and longer valid extensions remain accepted when transport limits permit and round-trip through supported bindings.
decisions.wire_consequences: Producers should stay within the twenty-character recommendation.
decisions.upstream_status: The recommendation is above the pinned 1.0.2 support line and is intentionally excluded from the accepted-clarification table.
decisions.reconsider_when: A supported stable CloudEvents release makes the first-character restriction normative or defines feature-line negotiation for it.

decisions.title: Data presence and JSON representation
interpretations: preserve presence and abstract data kind
reject data without an explicit content type
decisions.peer_behavior: Official Go and JavaScript SDK interoperability accepts ordinary JSON and binary data, but their in-memory zero-value models are not a normative presence contract for this package.
decisions.rationale: base64 must be canonical padded RFC 4648 encoding
decisions.security_consequences: Canonical base64 and explicit presence prevent alternate encodings and nil/empty confusion at authorization, hashing, or storage boundaries.
decisions.resource_consequences: Payload bytes, decoded bytes, and JSON depth are bounded before retention.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Round trips preserve whether data exists, its runtime kind, and which wire member represents it.
decisions.wire_consequences: other non-JSON types decode as binary.
decisions.reconsider_when: CloudEvents changes data-presence semantics, introduces another JSON payload member, or standardizes a different binary conversion rule.

decisions.title: Unknown extension abstract types
decisions.issue: A JSON string can represent CloudEvents String, Binary, URI, URI-reference, or Timestamp.
interpretations: decode unknown JSON strings as String while retaining Boolean and Integer types exactly
decisions.peer_behavior: SDKs preserve unknown extension values through their own type models, which differ by language.
decisions.selected_behavior: Unknown JSON Boolean and Integer values preserve those abstract types.
decisions.rationale: An unknown JSON string becomes String.
decisions.security_consequences: No syntax-based type confusion, URI resolution, timestamp parsing, or network access occurs for unknown extensions.
decisions.resource_consequences: Attribute counts, names, values, and integer range remain bounded.
decisions.wire_consequences: Applications needing stronger semantics must register or construct that extension explicitly rather than relying on decoder heuristics.
decisions.upstream_status: CloudEvents defines the abstract types but does not provide a registry-driven inference algorithm for unknown JSON extensions.
decisions.reconsider_when: CloudEvents publishes normative extension type discovery or the package introduces an explicit caller-supplied extension registry.

decisions.title: Duplicate and null context attributes
decisions.issue: Generic JSON and transport APIs can expose duplicate field names or repeated singleton headers, and optional JSON attributes may be null.
interpretations: reject every duplicate while treating null optional attributes as absent and null required attributes as invalid
decisions.peer_behavior: JSON and HTTP libraries vary in duplicate handling, and SDKs may normalize values into maps before application code sees them.
decisions.selected_behavior: Duplicate context attributes are rejected in JSON, HTTP, and Kafka even when values match.
decisions.rationale: Their normalization is not imported as a wire acceptance rule.
decisions.security_consequences: Rejection prevents shadowing and parser differentials.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Ambiguous messages fail instead of being normalized.
decisions.wire_consequences: Canonical valid messages remain interoperable with official Go and JavaScript SDK fixtures.
decisions.reconsider_when: A supported CloudEvents binding defines deterministic repeated-value semantics that cannot be represented by this singleton model.

decisions.title: URI and URI-reference input strictness
decisions.issue: Generic URI parsers may accept spaces or Unicode and silently percent-encode them.
decisions.peer_behavior: Language URI libraries differ in permissiveness and normalization.
decisions.selected_behavior: URI and URI-reference attribute values must already be valid RFC 3986 ASCII serialization.
decisions.rationale: CloudEvents SDK interoperability does not define one cross-language repair algorithm.
decisions.security_consequences: Strict validation prevents Unicode and percent-encoding aliases without performing I/O.
decisions.resource_consequences: URI bytes remain subject to the ordinary attribute-value limit.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Invalid or non-ASCII URI text is rejected instead of rewritten.
decisions.wire_consequences: Valid relative and absolute references preserve their exact serialized identity.
decisions.upstream_status: RFC 3986 supplies syntax; automatic IRI conversion and network resolution are outside the CloudEvents core contract.
decisions.reconsider_when: CloudEvents adopts an IRI profile or defines a canonical normalization algorithm for context attributes.

decisions.title: Deterministic JSON bytes
decisions.issue: CloudEvents requires JSON semantics but does not define object-member order, insignificant whitespace, timestamp normalization, or a general canonicalization profile.
interpretations: define a narrow deterministic package profile without changing CloudEvents semantics
decisions.peer_behavior: Official Go and JavaScript SDKs emit semantically interoperable JSON but do not promise byte identity with this package.
decisions.selected_behavior: Encoding emits context members in lexicographic order, no package-added insignificant whitespace, UTC RFC 3339 timestamps with only necessary fractional digits, base-10 integers, and padded RFC 4648 base64.
decisions.rationale: This is a Golib byte-stability contract, not CloudEvents or RFC 8785 conformance.
decisions.security_consequences: Deterministic output avoids hash and signature ambiguity.
decisions.resource_consequences: Encoding validates the event first and returns bounded owned bytes without executing extensions or resolving schemas.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Semantically equivalent package events produce stable package bytes.
decisions.wire_consequences: Other conforming serializers may produce different bytes and remain interoperable after decoding.
decisions.upstream_status: CloudEvents specifies the JSON mapping but no canonical-byte profile; this additional contract is package-owned.
decisions.reconsider_when: CloudEvents adopts a canonicalization profile or byte-level interoperability requires a versioned alternative serializer.

decisions.title: Structured metadata conflicts and mode selection
decisions.issue: Structured messages can carry redundant protocol metadata, singleton fields may repeat with different casing, and an unsupported structured media type could be misread as a binary event.
interpretations: Ignore all protocol metadata in structured mode
validate redundant metadata and reject every conflict or unsupported structured format
decisions.peer_behavior: HTTP stacks normalize header names differently, and SDKs vary in whether redundant structured metadata remains visible.
decisions.selected_behavior: Header names compare case-insensitively and singleton occurrences must be unique.
decisions.rationale: The bindings do not define a permissive conflict-recovery algorithm.
decisions.security_consequences: Fail-closed selection prevents metadata shadowing and content-type confusion.
decisions.resource_consequences: Header names, values, counts, total bytes, body bytes, and JSON depth are bounded before retained copies are created.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Canonical binary and structured messages interoperate normally.
decisions.wire_consequences: Ambiguous duplicates, conflicting metadata, and unsupported structured formats are rejected rather than normalized.
decisions.upstream_status: Binding files and official receiver scenarios
decisions.reconsider_when: A supported binding defines precedence for redundant structured metadata or registers another structured event format implemented by this package.

decisions.title: HTTP body presence, ownership, and cancellation
decisions.issue: An empty HTTP body can mean absent data or present empty data, and a decoder cannot forcibly cancel an arbitrary blocking reader without starting unmanaged work or owning the transport resource.
interpretations: Treat every empty body as absent
treat every empty body as present
spawn a goroutine to force cancellation
use content metadata for presence while preserving caller ownership and cooperative cancellation
decisions.peer_behavior: HTTP clients and SDK adapters own different body lifecycles.
decisions.resource_consequences: Body size is bounded with overflow-safe accounting.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Empty payload presence is deterministic from received metadata and JSON cannot be represented by an empty body.
decisions.wire_consequences: Strict HTTP encoding rejects present data without a declared content type because an untyped body cannot preserve its runtime kind.
decisions.upstream_status: CloudEvents defines binary mapping; reader ownership and forced-cancellation mechanics are package and Go runtime concerns.
decisions.reconsider_when: The decoder accepts a transport type whose close and cancellation lifecycle it explicitly owns.

decisions.title: Kafka tombstones, keys, and batch scope
decisions.issue: A nil Kafka value is a tombstone on compacted topics, while an empty non-nil value is distinct.
decisions.peer_behavior: Official Go and JavaScript SDK fixtures interoperate for canonical binary and structured records.
decisions.selected_behavior: Absent binary event data encodes as a nil record value and therefore a tombstone; present empty data encodes as non-nil zero-length bytes.
decisions.security_consequences: Key bytes, header names, values, total metadata, event bytes, and copied transport headers are bounded before retention.
decisions.resource_consequences: No broker I/O, partition selection, offset management, retry, or acknowledgement occurs.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Tombstone semantics remain visible rather than collapsing into empty data.
decisions.upstream_status: The Kafka binding and selected partitioning extension
decisions.reconsider_when: CloudEvents publishes a stable Kafka batch binding or changes absent-data and partition-key semantics.

decisions.title: Explicit schema validation without implicit I/O
decisions.issue: CloudEvents does not require receivers to fetch it
interpretations: validate only when a caller supplies an explicit validator
embed one schema engine and policy in the core
decisions.peer_behavior: SDKs commonly expose schema metadata without mandatory validation.
decisions.selected_behavior: Constructing or decoding an event never resolves a schema or performs network I/O.
decisions.rationale: Implicit validation during decoding would add hidden I/O and application policy.
decisions.security_consequences: Core decode has no SSRF, DNS, credential, cache, or remote-resource side effect.
decisions.resource_consequences: The package preserves cancellation and does not leak aliased payload storage.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Schema metadata round-trips whether or not validation is configured.
decisions.wire_consequences: Applications opt into validation explicitly and can change validators without changing wire decoding.
decisions.upstream_status: CloudEvents provides schema identity but no mandatory retrieval or validation algorithm; the no-I/O default is package-owned.
decisions.reconsider_when: CloudEvents publishes normative schema retrieval and validation behavior or the core adopts an explicit resolver interface with equivalent fail-closed policy.

decisions.title: Distributed tracing lifecycle ownership
decisions.issue: The extension requires multi-hop trace lifecycle behavior but the transport-independent event model does not own span creation or hop boundaries.
interpretations: rewrite tracing metadata during every codec operation
require applications and adapters to own explicit propagation policy
decisions.peer_behavior: SDK and telemetry integrations attach tracing lifecycle policy at different boundaries.
decisions.selected_behavior: The core validates traceparent and tracestate without starting spans or rewriting valid metadata.
decisions.rationale: Single-hop propagation is explicit and multi-hop lifecycle compliance is not claimed by the core codec.
decisions.security_consequences: Untrusted tracing values are grammar-checked before retention.
decisions.resource_consequences: Validation performs no telemetry I/O or background work.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Existing valid tracing attributes round-trip unchanged.
decisions.wire_consequences: Applications must preserve the starting trace across hops through their owned propagation boundary.
decisions.upstream_status: The pinned extension defines lifecycle requirements but no transport-independent Go ownership model.
decisions.reconsider_when: The core adopts an explicit tracing lifecycle abstraction or the extension revises multi-hop ownership.
